readerPromise: Examine the material and institutional supports that let moral commitments and historical memory persist.
protectedRevelations: Later strategic conclusions and normative prescriptions

authorReview.scope: Complete eight-sentence script checked against canonical short-reader opening evidence for premise, clear identity, specific interest and protected revelations.

authorReview.emotion: Concrete recognition, thoughtful tension and open curiosity; no melodramatic mystery or inflated promise.

independentReview.notes: Every spoken sentence reviewed against canonical English short reader for clear newcomer meaning, source grounding, curiosity and emotional intent. Replaced abstract promotional commentary with concrete viewer-facing language. All eight sentences have a distinct intended response and explicit restrained TTS direction; fictional later outcomes remain withheld. This is editorial review, not audience testing or rendered-audio approval.

sentenceIntentions.text: A government changes a map, and a destroyed village becomes merely an abandoned settlement.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Show administrative wording rewriting a village's destruction
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Feel the force of a seemingly small map change

sentenceIntentions.text: Eden Was a Jungle opens with an archivist facing that apparently administrative correction.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Name the archivist and political inquiry
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Understand the concrete opening rather than expecting a jungle adventure

sentenceIntentions.text: The example opens a political question about what our moral promises need in order to survive.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Connect the example with durable moral commitments
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: See why memory needs more than admirable language

sentenceIntentions.text: A record can preserve a truth without giving anyone the power to act on it.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Separate preserved truth from power to act

sentenceIntentions.text: The book follows the money, institutions, and sometimes uncomfortable protections behind rights and public memory.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Introduce the resources and protections behind rights

sentenceIntentions.text: It asks what happens when a society praises its ideals while overlooking the arrangements that sustain them.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Expose praise that overlooks supporting arrangements
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Question a society's confidence in its own ideals

sentenceIntentions.text: Good principles feel less secure when the people and records protecting them become vulnerable.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Feel the difficulty of sustaining moral commitments

sentenceIntentions.text: Begin with the two maps on the archivist’s desk, and follow what changes when the older one disappears.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Return to the two maps and possible disappearance
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Want to know what the archivist's choice can preserve
